subject: DPA: data provenance & tiered-retention Q&A
messages:
From: Anna Perez <anna@medicom.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medicom.com
Date: Tue, 07 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: data provenance & tiered-retention questions

Hi Rafael / Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. As our security team reviews the retention and deletion clauses we have a few focused questions so we can propose redlines back to counsel quickly: 

1) Provenance / Processing locus — can you confirm which processing steps for inference (prompt pre-processing, model execution, telemetry) will occur inside vs outside the US region when we select "US-only" residency? Is there any asynchronous replication to non-US support regions for debugging/ops?

2) Backup & snapshots — what is Redwood's default backup tier and retention for customer data that is subject to the DPA? Is there a separate onshore backup option, and how is it triggered (config vs contract)?

3) Cache / ephemeral stores — our lawyers want explicit limits for KV cache and ephemeral logs that might contain derived data. Can you provide TTLs and an operational path for certified deletion (proof to customer) for those caches?

4) Evidence of deletion — we need a short playbook to show to auditors: when we serve an erasure request, what artifacts do you produce (audit log extract, tombstone manifest, storage deletion record)?

If you can answer these at a high level we will translate into exact clause asks. We have an internal timeline to return redlines by Friday COB PT.

Best,
Anna
Anna Perez
Security Manager, Medicom Health

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Anna Perez <anna@medicom.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 May 2029 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data provenance & tiered-retention questions

Anna — thanks for the specific asks. Attached are two artifacts that should help: a PDF with our annotated DPA (Redline_DPA_RM_v2.pdf) and a region/dataflow diagram (Redwood-dataflow-region.png). High-level answers below; happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer.

1) Processing locus
- Control plane metadata (account management, billing) may cross into our global control plane for operational alerts; customer data for inference (prompts, responses, embeddings) is processed in the selected region by default.
- We do not perform asynchronous replication of inference payloads to other regions for normal operations. Exception: cross-region replication can occur for disaster recovery (DR) only if both parties agree and it is contractually enabled.

2) Backups & snapshots
- Default snapshot cadence: daily logical metadata + weekly full snapshot (retention 30 days by default for hosted customers).
- Onshore backup option: available as an addendum (Reserved or Private deployments) — we can commit to storing backups only in US zones when that option is selected in the contract.

3) Cache / ephemeral stores
- KV cache TTL: default 24 hours; configurable per-customer with min allowed 0 (ephemeral).
- Ephemeral logs: debug traces are kept for 7 days in production by default; PII/PHI redaction hooks run before any long-term storage. We can extend redaction or shorten TTLs for Medicom under a contract clause.

4) Evidence of deletion
- Operational artifacts we provide: deletion request audit (request id + timestamp), storage object deletion markers (object IDs and deletion timestamps), and a generated erasure manifest (file) summarizing affected objects/paths. For backup snapshots, we provide a snapshot purge confirmation when snapshot TTLs are removed.

Proposed next step: Laura drafted a short compromise paragraph we often use to close these topics (attached in the redline). If Medicom needs formal wording for the DPA appendix (e.g., an Annex B for residency/backup handling), we can supply that text for insertion.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Anna Perez <anna@medicom.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: John Harper <john.harper@medicom.com>, security@medicom.com
Date: Wed, 08 May 2029 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data provenance & tiered-retention questions

Rafael — appreciate the detail. A couple follow-ups from our counsel/security: 

• Offsite DR: John asked whether DR replication would create additional retention obligations outside the geographic boundary and whether you support a short list of permitted DR regions (we prefer explicit 'US-only' DR for Medicom).

• Deletion proof granularity: auditors typically want a per-object deletion id + hash + timestamp. Will your erasure manifest include object hashes or only object IDs?

• Legal hold: how is legal hold handled for backups/snapshots? If we put a hold, can you suspend purge jobs without impacting other tenants?

If you can respond to those three points we can incorporate concrete redlines.

Thanks,
Anna

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 May 2029 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data provenance & tiered-retention questions (internal)

Team — drafting a concise clause we can offer as a compromise. Pulling from the redline and Rafael's notes, draft below for review before we send back to Medicom counsel: 

"Annex B — Residency, Backups and Erasure
1. Residency: Customer Data subject to this Agreement shall be processed and stored in the U.S. geographic region selected by Customer. Redwood may route only control-plane metadata outside the region for operational purposes; no customer content shall be replicated outside the U.S. except for disaster recovery explicitly requested and agreed in writing.
2. Backups: Redwood shall maintain daily and weekly snapshots as configured. For customers requiring U.S.-only backups, Redwood shall store backups in U.S. zones exclusively where the onshore backup addendum is executed. Backup retention for hosted customers is thirty (30) days unless otherwise specified in the Order Form.
3. Ephemeral stores and cache: Redwood will minimize retention of ephemeral caches used for inference. Default KV cache TTL is twenty-four (24) hours; Customer may elect a shorter TTL where operationally feasible.
4. Erasure and evidence: Upon validated deletion request, Redwood will provide an erasure manifest containing object identifiers, deletion timestamps and an associated audit request identifier. For backup snapshots subject to deletion, Redwood will provide a purge confirmation indicating affected snapshot IDs and timestamps.

Please confirm if this language covers the core asks — if Medicom needs hashes included in the manifest we can add a line, though that will alter how we store snapshot metadata.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Anna Perez <anna@medicom.com>, John Harper <john.harper@medicom.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 May 2029 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final proposal: Annex B wording + operational notes

Anna / John — thanks for the quick turnaround. Laura's draft below is our proposed compromise. A couple of practical notes to set expectations operationally: 

• DR: If Medicom requires US-only DR, we will enable a policy that restricts DR replicas to a pre-approved list of U.S. regions. That configuration is an operational addendum and will be listed in the Order Form.

• Hashes in manifest: we can include object hashes in the erasure manifest, but full per-object hashing of large snapshot sets can add up to a multi-hour job to churn on purge. If Medicom elects hashes, we recommend limiting hashes to critical objects or a sampling approach; we can commit to a documented SLA for manifest generation time.

• Legal hold: when a legal hold is placed Redwood will suspend purge jobs for affected snapshots/objects and mark them as "hold" in the manifest. Holds are scoped to the customer's tenant and will not impact unrelated tenants.

If that sounds acceptable we will return the Annex B text in a format that counsel can insert directly into the DPA and flag a couple of redlines in the PDF. Would you like us to prepare two options (with and without hashes) for your counsel to choose from?

Best regards,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
